title: Anonymous appliance retailer stimulus (CXL description research): hedonic product copy (flat)
company: Anonymous appliance retailer stimulus (CXL description research)

change.control: Utilitarian description of the vacuum, emphasizing technical utility.
change.variant: Reword the same features of the vacuum as pleasure/benefit-oriented hedonic copy; remove prices, logos and irrelevant information.

quote: While the utilitarian product description did elicit a higher perceived value, the difference was not significant.
notes: Vacuum bargain-question p=0.69; too-expensive p=0.84. Valuation favored utilitarian text without significance. 304 survey participants across the study, not a published per-arm count. No purchases measured; household appliances only.
